title: Exact support uncertainty and a sealed Bell-data test
description:
An exact support-uncertainty theorem holds at every generated binary depth: the occupied point and Walsh-mode counts obey s_t s_f ≥ 2^d.

Maria Smith derives phase-count orthogonality, the Parseval energy identity, the support-product inequality and cancellation of every positive rational spacing. The complete depth-one through depth-four census contains 65,808 nonempty supports and 372 saturated cases. Complete joint-support classifications distinguish factorability from carrier size; sixteen local Bell response records establish the three-of-four bound.

A separately sealed comparison with Storz et al.’s superconducting-circuit Bell experiment retains the entire measured interval 2.0714–2.0780 above the local bound two, central excess above twenty-two uncertainties, more than one million trials, reported P below 10^−108 and a positive worst-edge locality margin of 1.814 ns. Full timing, memory and measurement-independence records and both rejection controls are included.

The paper contains the complete mathematical derivations, exhaustive grammars, original experimental conditions, native Lean proof references and 628 audited declarations with empty axiom dependencies. Source and evidence archive includes exact reproduction and pinned V3/V4 correspondence. Scientific author: Maria Smith, Ernos Labs.
